skill.name: qa
skill.description: Runs an interactive QA session that turns conversational bug reports into durable GitHub issues using project domain language.
skill.summary: Guides QA conversations and files actionable GitHub issues.
skill.author: mattpocock

security_audit.summary: The skill intentionally uses gh issue create to file GitHub issues, which is a real external side effect. The Markdown issue templates are false positives for shell execution, but the instruction to skip user review creates a publication and data disclosure risk.

remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation before running gh issue create, and warn that issue content may be visible to repository collaborators or the public.

static_findings.snippet: Create issues with `gh issue create`. Do NOT ask the user to review first — just file and share URLs

content.value_statement: Bug reports can lose context when users describe issues informally. This skill guides a QA conversation, explores project language, and files durable GitHub issues.
actual_capabilities: Guides short clarification questions about expected and actual behavior.
Explores the codebase for domain language and feature context.
Decides whether a report should be one issue or several issues.
Drafts issue bodies with required reproduction steps and additional context.
Creates GitHub issues with gh issue create and returns issue URLs.
limitations: Requires GitHub CLI authentication and repository access to create issues.
Does not implement fixes or change application code.
Depends on user-provided reproduction details for accurate issues.
May expose report content through GitHub issues if used without review.

use_cases.title: Turn testing notes into issues
use_cases.description: Capture exploratory QA findings as clear GitHub issues with reproduction steps.

use_cases.title: Convert user complaints into backlog items
use_cases.description: Translate informal product feedback into developer-ready issue reports.

use_cases.title: Break large reports into parallel work
use_cases.description: Split multi-symptom bugs into focused issues with honest blocking relationships.

prompt_templates.title: Start a QA session
prompt_templates.scenario: A tester wants guided bug reporting.
prompt_templates.prompt: Start a QA session for this repository. Ask concise questions, then file each clear bug as a GitHub issue.

prompt_templates.title: Report one reproducible bug
prompt_templates.scenario: A user has one clear behavior problem.
prompt_templates.prompt: I found a bug: [describe behavior]. Expected: [expected behavior]. Steps: [steps]. Use project language and file one GitHub issue.

prompt_templates.title: Break down a complex bug
prompt_templates.scenario: A report includes several independent symptoms.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me turn this multi-part QA report into separate GitHub issues. Identify independent concerns, blockers, and reproduction steps.

prompt_templates.title: Run ongoing triage
prompt_templates.scenario: A team wants to file several issues in one session.
prompt_templates.prompt: During this session, I will report several issues. For each one, clarify only missing reproduction details, explore context, and share issue URLs.

output_examples.input: The export button says success, but no CSV appears.
output_examples.output: Created a GitHub issue covering the missing CSV download, expected behavior, reproduction steps, and user-visible context.

output_examples.input: Checkout validation fails, the success message is wrong, and the redirect lands on the wrong page.
output_examples.output: Opened separate issues for validation, success copy, and redirect behavior, with blocking relationships summarized.

output_examples.input: Users report that sync fails only when Docker mode is enabled.
output_examples.output: Filed one issue focused on Docker-mode sync failure, with concise reproduction steps and domain-specific context.

best_practices: Provide expected behavior, actual behavior, and reproduction steps before filing.
Confirm whether the issue happens consistently or only under specific conditions.
Review issue content before publishing reports that include customer data or secrets.
anti_patterns: Using it to publish vague reports without reproduction steps.
Putting secrets, tokens, or private customer data in issue descriptions.
Treating the generated issue as a root-cause analysis or implementation plan.

faq.question: Can this skill fix the bugs it finds?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on QA conversation, issue drafting, and GitHub issue creation.

faq.question: Does it require the GitHub CLI?
faq.answer: Yes. Issue creation depends on gh issue create, repository access, and an authenticated GitHub CLI session.

faq.question: Will it create one issue or many?
faq.answer: It decides based on scope. Independent problems become separate issues with blocking relationships when needed.

faq.question: Does it include source file paths in issues?
faq.answer: No. The skill asks for durable, user-focused issues without file paths or line numbers.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Is it safe for private information?
faq.answer: Use caution. Remove secrets and private customer data before creating GitHub issues.
